hero.headline: Fort Pierce tightens Flock camera rules after ex-officer charged in tracking case
hero.teaser: The Fort Pierce Police Department is implementing tighter restrictions on its Flock license plate reader system after former officer Josepher Crutchfield was arrested on four felony charges for allegedly tracking his ex-girlfriend through the databases.
hero.body:
The Fort Pierce Police Department is tightening access rules for its Flock license plate reader system after former officer Josepher Crutchfield was arrested on four felony counts of unauthorized computer access for allegedly tracking his ex-girlfriend through law enforcement databases. Crutchfield is scheduled to appear in court Wednesday on charges stemming from investigators' findings that he searched his ex-girlfriend's vehicle in the Flock system 382 times between October and his arrest, part of more than 400 total database searches.

 A judge denied a bond reduction request for Crutchfield, who remains held at the St. Lucie County Jail. The felony charges relate to his alleged misuse of the Flock camera system and other police databases to monitor his former girlfriend's movements and location.

 Chief David Smith is involved in implementing the new policy restrictions on Flock camera access in response to the case. The department's previous access protocols allowed Crutchfield to conduct hundreds of searches before the misuse was detected.

 Crutchfield was previously suspended for two days in 2021 for sexually harassing female Fort Pierce police employees. That earlier disciplinary action preceded the database misuse investigation that led to his arrest this week on the four felony counts.

Charles, who has taught at the school for nearly a decade, uses survivor stories, images, and audio recordings to help students understand a day they never lived through.
